![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211556/assets/eb5f10ce887ba9d167b2753618064fcdbf8d1f42371d733aacd56a8d8cb5e667.png)

Let $X$ and $Y$ be continuous random variables with the joint probability density function 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}, & (x,y)\in D, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

If $F(x,y)$ is the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y,$ find $F(1,\frac{1}{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are continuous random variables with the joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the corresponding joint CDF is given by

$$
F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{y}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(u,v)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v.
$$

Let's draw the point $(1,\frac{1}{2})$ on our diagram. Let's also consider the region $Δ$ that lies below and to the left of this point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14211556/assets/53d0466b98c4b9b2704cc2f7610e7f28cee6ec27aaf2ea94be75c5b3f32a8257.png)

Using the definition of the joint CDF, we have

$$
F(1,\frac{1}{2})=P(X<1,Y<\frac{1}{2})={\int }_{-\infty }^{1/2}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1}f(u,v)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v.
$$

For the purposes of computation, we're only interested in the region inside $Δ$ where $f(x,y)$ is nonzero. This is given by

$$
D\cap Δ=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 1,\,0\le y\le \frac{1}{2}\}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1/2}{\int }_{-\infty }^{1}f(u,v)\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(\frac{9}{2}{u}^{2}{v}^{2})\,\text{d}u\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}{[\frac{3}{2}{u}^{3}{v}^{2}]}_{u=-1}^{u=1}\,\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}[\frac{3}{2}{v}^{2}-(-\frac{3}{2}{v}^{2})]\text{d}v \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1/2}3{v}^{2}\text{d}v \\  & ={[{v}^{3}]}_{v=0}^{v=1/2} \\  & =\frac{1}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
